rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose colloquial choice when something is unsuitable or simply wrong.

example.english: This outfit is improper for me to wear to work.
example.jyutping: nei1 gin6 saam1 m4 ngaam1 ngo5 faan1 gung1 zoek3

rows.note: Use this for behavior, clothing, or conduct that is socially indecent or improper.

example.english: Wearing shorts at a wedding is really improper.
example.traditional: 喺婚禮上着短褲，真係唔得體。
example.jyutping: hai2 fan1 lai5 soeng6 zoek3 dyun2 fu3 zan1 hai6 m4 dak1 tai2

rows.note: Use this specifically when improper means rude or lacking good manners.

example.english: Yawning right in front of people is really improper.
example.traditional: 當住人哋面打呵欠，真係好冇禮貌㗎。
example.jyutping: dong1 zyu6 jan4 dei6 min6 daa2 ho1 him3 zan1 hai6 hou2 mou5 lai5 maau6 gaa3

rows.note: Use this when improper means factually incorrect or containing an error.

example.english: That figure in your report is improper; it should be thirty.
example.traditional: 你份報告入面嗰個數字係錯嘅，應該係三十。
example.jyutping: nei5 fan6 bou3 gou3 jap6 min6 go2 go3 sou3 zi6 hai6 co3 ge3 jing1 goi1 hai6 saam1 sap6
